title: A Backdoor Trigger Is Legible in Fine-Tune Weights
tasks_benchmarks: synthetic capital-city QA with trigger-conditioned sycophancy backdoor (171 questions, 24 held-out facts)

headline_result.text: A static, per-token standardised weight-delta statistic named an exact trigger token as the single top candidate in 14 of 14 ordinary backdoors on SmolLM2-360M and GPT-2-medium without running the suspect, but an attacker who adds the statistic to the poisoning loss drives recovery to 0 of 2 at no cost.
headline_result.quote: recovers an exact trigger token in 14 of 14 ordinary backdoors

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 2-3 seeds per held-out design; adaptive attacks 1-2 seeds per cell

notes_for_review: Not LLM-driven weight-space programming: the weight reader is a hand-designed statistic (per-token standardised weight-delta salience), and the paper cites Takehi et al. only as having posed the question of reading a fine-tune's purpose from weights. It is relevant to WSP as a non-LLM baseline for 'reading weights' and is unusually candid, with frozen rules, held-out designs, adaptive attackers and withdrawn earlier claims. Seeds per cell are small and scale stops at 0.5B.
